source_windows: All twenty original 65x65 Float32 source windows, unchanged source pixels, BNG origins, metre/ODN metadata conventions and warnings. No favourable site selection.
unit_cell_identity: For an original 1x1 source cell, both P1 diagonals have squared L2 error mixed_coefficient^2/90 and maximum error abs(mixed_coefficient)/4 at its centre. Use this verified analytic identity for both orientations to avoid floating quadrature noise inventing fine-cell orientation switches.
p1_selection: Choose the lower integrated local L2-squared error of the two possible P1 rectangle diagonals. A fixed numerical tie guard of 64*Float64 epsilon*max(1, local squared errors) prefers the existing minus diagonal when values differ only within that guard; this prevents theoretically identical fine-cell errors creating spurious orientation records. Costs include each change of contiguous triangle-strip orientation.
hybrid_selection: Choose the lower integrated local L2-squared error of bilinear ruled, minus-diagonal P1, plus-diagonal P1. The same fixed numerical tie guard prefers ruled, then minus, then plus. Local selections are within the stated floating guard of the numerical minimum, not an exact-arithmetic optimality proof. Every orientation/type run, shared Float64 XYZ, header and index byte counts.
selection: For each family/byte ceiling, choose minimum whole-domain E2 among all 49 feasible grids, then complete bytes, nx, ny. For each maximum-error target, choose minimum complete bytes among feasible grids, then E2, nx, ny. Missing target models and all losing outcomes remain explicit.
metrics: Whole-domain E2 of the saved native function against the original piecewise-bilinear Float32 reference. Exact degree-appropriate source-cell integration; check original source-cell corners and interior quadratic extrema on both possible triangle diagonals. Guard 1e-9 + max source absolute z * 1e-12 m. Not surveyed ground truth or interval proof.
continuity: One integer tensor grid, identical shared corner heights and linear rectangle-boundary functions; both diagonal orientations and ruled cells join C0 without T-junctions. Gradients may jump.
reporting: Retain all 1960 new saved models, all 200 byte-ceiling comparisons and 120 target comparisons, including pure-triangle choices, missing models, ties, extra orientation overhead and unfavourable results. Prior fixed-diagonal P1, ruled and two-way mixture reports remain immutable and separately identified. This strengthens the fixed-grid triangle control, not the paper's adaptive greedy algorithm or ArcGIS software. No runtime or globally optimal-mesh claim.
